learning_outcomes.text: The goal of the course is to convey to students the fundamentals of fluid mechanics – statics and dynamics of fluids. The basic laws of motion of liquids and gases are discussed. Starting with the basic laws of hydrostatics and aerostatics, the kinematics of fluids and the general conservation laws of mass, energy, momentum, and angular momentum of fluids are derived. Simplifications and application areas of the streamline theory are explained. Building on the global consideration, local flow phenomena, such as laminar and turbulent flow, flow around bodies, and the fundamentals of boundary layer theory are presented. Finally, the behavior of compressible flow is considered using the model fluid of an ideal gas.
Independently work on fundamental fluid mechanics problems for incompressible and simple compressible fluids.
Make an estimation and classification of the essential conditions and boundary conditions when applying the conservation laws for mass, energy, and momentum.
Perform an initial assessment and classification of local flow phenomena in internal flow (pipe flow) and external flow around bodies and simple systems.
Distinguish the characteristics of incompressible and compressible fluid flow.

syllabus_topics: Pipe flow and flow around bodies
Drag and Lift of bodies in flow
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded for passing the written exam. The importance of the grade for the final grade is determined by the Bachelor's examination regulations.
